input: Audience: Wedding-business owners already investing in paid ads who want to reduce spend but do not yet have clear evidence about which channel or lead source is working better. | Tension: The owner wants a lower bill, while a sharp reduction could make it harder to assess the new campaign and channel mix. | Argument: When traffic rises without clearly stronger leads, reducing spend need not mean making the largest possible cut. A more measured reset can preserve room to compare channels and reassess the budget against conversion and lead-quality evidence. | Take: Treat the first revised budget as a provisional test, not a proven optimum: choose a reduction that fits the business, then review the resulting conversion and lead-quality evidence before reallocating. | Mechanism: In this account discussion, the owner reported increased traffic without clearly stronger leads. The team recommended a lower Google Ads budget than the existing spend, an initially fairly even Google and Meta split, and later reallocation based on data. The recommendation connected budget restraint to a plan for comparison rather than an assumption that more traffic meant better leads. | Reader decision: Before cutting spend, decide what budget is sustainable for an initial test and what conversion or lead-quality evidence would justify changing the channel allocation.
